# Error reporting

Rust reports type errors while compiling definitions. Failures that depend on
Nix evaluation are reported by Rusix with the original Nix reason and recovered
Rust source locations.

The examples below are actual outputs from the repository's diagnostic fixtures.
They illustrate errors reported during evaluation. The Rust excerpts show the
relevant definitions; complete fixtures are linked in each section.

## Conflicting NixOS definitions

Two modules define different values for the same OpenSSH option. NixOS rejects
the combination. The [merge fixture](../crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/merge_fixtures.rs)
creates the contributions in separate functions:

```rust
pub fn a() -> NixosModule {
    NixosModule::new(
        Config::new().set_dynamic("services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser", "root"),
    )
}

pub fn b() -> NixosModule {
    NixosModule::new(
        Config::new().set_dynamic("services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser", "nobody"),
    )
}
```

The Nix evaluator reports generated definition markers in its reason. This is an
excerpt from its output, with the longer trace omitted:

```text
The option `services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser' has conflicting definition values:
- In `rn-35ddcb8630f9fcc5': "nobody"
- In `rn-979317c120ec6487': "root"
Use `lib.mkForce value` or `lib.mkDefault value` to change the priority on any of these definitions.
```

Rusix resolves those markers to the Rust definitions and renders both locations:

```text
error[nixos-merge]: conflicting definitions for a NixOS option

  --> crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/merge_fixtures.rs:16:23
   |
 16 |         Config::new().set_dynamic("services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser", "nobody"),
   |                       ^
   = origin: set services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser
   = conflicting definition

  --> crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/merge_fixtures.rs:10:23
   |
 10 |         Config::new().set_dynamic("services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser", "root"),
   |                       ^
   = origin: set services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser
   = conflicting definition

   = option: services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser
   = Nix: The option `services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser' has conflicting definition values:
     - In `Rust crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/merge_fixtures.rs:16:23': "nobody"
     - In `Rust crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/merge_fixtures.rs:10:23': "root"
     Use `lib.mkForce value` or `lib.mkDefault value` to change the priority on any of these definitions.
```

These are two views of the same failure in a Rust-generated module. The original
Nix output remains available in `nix.stderr`; the Rust-facing report translates
source markers while retaining the option and underlying reason.

## An invalid option value

The [type fixture](../crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/nixos_fixtures.rs) deliberately uses
`Config::set_dynamic` to supply a string where NixOS expects a port number.
Its relevant assignment is:

```rust
Config::new().set_dynamic("services.openssh.ports", vec!["twenty-two"]);
```

The dynamic API allows this Rust value to reach NixOS. A Rust model with a
`Vec<u16>` field would reject the string during compilation. Here, NixOS performs
the option check, and Rusix identifies the assignment that supplied the value:

```text
error[nixos-type]: NixOS rejected an option value
  --> crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/nixos_fixtures.rs:13:18
   |
 13 |                 .set_dynamic("services.openssh.ports", vec!["twenty-two"]),
   |                  ^
   = origin: set services.openssh.ports
   = option: services.openssh.ports
   = Nix: A definition for option `services.openssh.ports."[definition 1-entry 1]"' is not of type `16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)'. Definition values:
     - In `Rust crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/nixos_fixtures.rs:13:18': "twenty-two"
```

The error retains NixOS's expected type and the rejected value, together with
the option path and Rust location.

## A deferred expression failure

The [nested fixture](../crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/fixtures.rs) contains a division
that Rust constructs as an expression for Nix to evaluate:

```rust
Config::new().set_dynamic(
    "services.openssh.ports",
    vec![Expr::int(22), Expr::int(44).divide(Expr::int(0))],
);
```

Nix points to the division in generated source. This trace excerpt has terminal
colors removed and the temporary directory replaced with `<session>`:

```text
       … while calling the 'div' builtin
         at <session>/generated.nix:2:41:
            1| # Generated by Rusix. Edit the Rust source.
            2| { "services"."openssh"."ports" = ([ 22 (builtins.div 44 0) ]); }
             |                                         ^
            3|

       error: division by zero
```

Rusix maps that generated position back to the Rust operation and recovers the
surrounding option path:

```text
error[nix-eval]: generated configuration was rejected by Nix
  --> crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/fixtures.rs:15:47
   |
 15 |             vec![Expr::int(22), Expr::int(44).divide(Expr::int(0))],
   |                                               ^
   = origin: integer division
   = option: services.openssh.ports
   = Nix: division by zero
```

The failure is inside a list, but the report points to `.divide()` rather than
only the list or its containing configuration.

## Where attribution stops

An error in an imported module may identify only the Rust import boundary.
The `external` fixture intentionally omits an upstream dependency:

```text
error[external-nix]: imported NixOS module evaluation failed
  --> crates/rusix/src/bin/cli/nixos_fixtures.rs:33:14
   |
 33 |             .import(ExistingModule::NixosLabel),
   |              ^
   = origin: import nixos/modules/misc/label.nix
   = option: system.nixos.label
   = imported Nix: nixos/modules/misc/label.nix
   = Nix: attribute 'version' missing
```

This identifies the import that introduced the failing module. It does not claim
that the Rust import is the precise cause of the missing upstream value.

When no Rust origin is available, the report says so. The `unmapped` fixture
injects an expression without source metadata:

```text
error[nix-eval]: generated configuration was rejected by Nix
   = Rust origin unavailable; inspect generated source and raw Nix diagnostic
   = Nix: backend failure without metadata
```

Other mappings can also be incomplete. NixOS may report only part of a merge
conflict, and upstream diagnostic format changes can affect recovery. See
[runtime diagnostics](runtime-diagnostics.md) for the mapping rules and limits.

## Reproduce the examples

Follow [repository setup](development.md#setup) to initialize the pinned sources.
From the repository root:

```bash
cargo run --locked -p rusix --features dev-cli -- check-nixos merge-two --out target/error-reporting/merge-two
cargo run --locked -p rusix --features dev-cli -- check-nixos type --out target/error-reporting/type
cargo run --locked -p rusix --features dev-cli -- check nested --out target/error-reporting/nested
cargo run --locked -p rusix --features dev-cli -- check-nixos external --out target/error-reporting/external
cargo run --locked -p rusix --features dev-cli -- check unmapped --out target/error-reporting/unmapped
```

Each command deliberately exits with status 1. The output directory contains
`diagnostic.txt` and `diagnostic.json`, together with the original `nix.stderr`.
See [diagnostic fixtures](development.md#diagnostic-fixtures) for the artifact layout.
